trends.name: Iran War Oil Supply Shock
trends.summary: Brent crude surged back above $100/barrel as Iran denies peace talks with the US. Oil supply shock quantified at 16MMB/d today declining to 10MMb/d in April. Multiple countries mediating US-Iran deal as geopolitical tensions reverberate globally, with Trump signaling intent to make a deal but no direct negotiations confirmed.

trends.name: Private Credit Funds Imploding
trends.summary: Apollo's private-credit fund and KKR/Future Standard fund both restricting investor redemptions with Moody's downgrading the latter to junk status due to growing bad loans. Software exposure in private credit portfolios is presenting systemic risks, with JPMorgan positioned to capitalize on the meltdown while banks face new counterparty risks.

trends.name: Labor Market Deterioration
trends.summary: Job postings on Indeed fell 5% YoY to lowest since October 2025, down 36% since April 2022 and now at February 2021 levels. Labor market softening signals economic slowdown ahead, with recession probability at 12% according to Goldman Sachs market-implied odds within the next year.

trends.name: Tech Supply Chain & Geopolitics
trends.summary: US bans all foreign-made network routers as part of broader supply chain security measures. Japan PM orders review of entire oil supply chain amid Iran war impacts. Nintendo cuts Switch 2 output over 30% on weak holiday sales, signaling demand weakness in consumer electronics.

trends.name: SoftBank OpenAI Mega-Bet & Borrowing Limits
trends.summary: SoftBank testing its own borrowing limits with $30 billion bet on OpenAI, raising questions about leverage risks amid tightening credit conditions. Move reflects AI investment mania but also signals potential strain on mega-cap tech valuations and credit availability.

trends.name: Credit Conditions Tightening Despite Rate Debate
trends.summary: While Fed rate hike timing remains debated, credit conditions are already tightening materially in real time. Rising oil prices and inflation concerns push central banks toward cautious policy stance, with ECB president comparing 2020s to 1920s, signaling stagflation risks.

trends.name: Asian Geopolitical De-escalation Relief
trends.summary: Asian equities rebounded after Trump signaled US delay on strikes against Iran's infrastructure, reducing immediate military escalation risk. However, multiple mediators working on deal without direct US-Iran negotiations confirms elevated geopolitical tail risks.

trends.name: EV Market Collapse & Battery Pivot
trends.summary: EV battery startup pivots to defense industry amid weak electric vehicle market demand. XPeng positioned as long-term strong buy but sector facing structural headwinds; Align Technology downgraded with only international growth possible. Market rotation away from EV hype toward defense/AI winners.

trends.name: M&A Activity in Banking & Luxury
trends.summary: Japan's second-largest bank considering Jefferies takeover amid consolidation pressures. Estée Lauder pursuing takeover talks with Puig (Charlotte Tilbury owner) as luxury sector consolidates; Puig stock surged 15% on confirmation. Strategic M&A signaling sector stress and capital reallocation.

trends.name: Inflation Pressures in Emerging Markets
trends.summary: Philippines warns higher inflation and declining remittances threaten economic growth targets; sustained oil rises to $128/barrel in Q2 2026 could trigger negative rating pressure on APAC sovereigns per Fitch. Emerging markets facing dual shock of commodity inflation and remittance decline.

trends.name: Industrial Incident & Refinery Risks
trends.summary: Reported explosion and fire at Valero oil refinery in Port Arthur, Texas with shelter-in-place advisories. Incident highlights physical supply risks amid geopolitical tensions, with oil infrastructure vulnerability potentially exacerbating supply shock concerns.

trends.name: Potential Market Manipulation & Insider Trading
trends.summary: $655k in 1-day-to-expiration puts loaded 2% out-of-the-money just 15 minutes before negative news broke on wires, suggesting possible pre-market insider information advantage. Raises regulatory concerns about market integrity and surveillance in high-frequency trading environments.
